title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Self-Represented Litigants in Negotiation
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: During settlement discussions, a self-represented defendant mistakenly believes they are legally liable for $10,000, whereas the law actually limits their liability to $2,000. The plaintiff's paralegal knows of the defendant's mistake. What must the paralegal do?
options: Draft a settlement for $10,000 immediately, as the paralegal owes no duty to the defendant.
Advise the defendant of the correct law to ensure fairness.
Not take unfair advantage of the unrepresented person's obvious mistake of law, ensure they know the paralegal does not protect their interests, and advise them to seek independent legal advice.
Withdraw from the file due to a conflict of interest.
questions.explain: Rule 4.05 states a paralegal dealing with an unrepresented person shall take care not to take unfair advantage of them, making it clear they do not represent them, and must urge them to get independent legal representation. While the paralegal cannot give legal advice, securing a highly disproportionate settlement by exploiting legal ignorance skirts the line of sharp practice and taking unfair advantage.
